prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: one motion sprite sheet for an exercise demonstration, 9 square cells in an exact 3x3 grid. Read left to right, top to bottom: the cells are consecutive poses of the SAME man using the SAME machine in ONE locked scene. Each cell has precisely the same camera, position, scale, shadows, lighting and full body/machine framing. No gutter, lines, borders, captions, numbers or arrows. A large square image, ideally 1536x1536 or higher, each cell square. Match the colored realistic exercise illustration of the references: muscular athletic adult man with natural warm skin, short dark hair, defined muscular legs/torso, charcoal shorts and black trainers. Reference 1 is machine/style guidance; reference 2 is character/skin/render style only (ignore the chest machine in reference 2). Off-white studio floor and background. Front camera only slightly 3/4 so both thighs, both knees and both pads remain visible. Seated upright, back and pelvis resting against seat/backrest; hands hold low fixed side handles, head/torso/pelvis/hands never move. A grey selectorized hip machine with a black padded chair and TWO separate hinged leg-pad lever assemblies with attached footrests, exactly the same shape in all cells. Every lever is rigid and pivots about its fixed mechanical hip hinge; no bending, changing thickness, vanishing supports or changing feet count. A safety cover encloses the weight stack so internal weights are not visible; cover, fixed base, seat and backrest must be pixel-consistent. No skin texture flicker, warping, thin anatomy, extra limbs, floating feet, intersecting legs or footrest. Whole machine and both shoes in every cell, with the same margins. Exercise: SEATED HIP ABDUCTION (cadeira ABDUTORA), moving the thighs OUTWARD against lateral pads. Exactly TWO broad black pads touch the OUTSIDE/lateral surfaces of the thighs just above the knees, never between the knees. The feet rest on the two lever footrests; knees remain bent about 90 degrees, feet directly below their respective knees. Start almost closed and progressively open both thighs symmetrically from the hip in 9 smooth monotonic steps. Nine cell poses with each thigh's angle away from the centerline: 1=5deg; 2=7deg; 3=12deg; 4=19deg; 5=27deg; 6=34deg; 7=40deg; 8=44deg; 9=45deg. The last cell is comfortably open, never a split. The pads and footrests follow each thigh rigidly. This sheet contains ONLY the opening phase, NOT a return phase. Do not repeat the same pose or open then close.
